2014_064_051514spmtg.paragraph: Agenda and backup materials for a special Troy Board of Education meeting held Thursday, May 15, 2014 at 4:45 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois. The board took up award of Bid Package 1 for secure entrances at 14 buildings, rescission of an earlier iPad case award to CDWG, purchase of MaxCase Shield cases instead, and adoption of the Oakland Schools biennial election resolution. The secure entrance award totaled $3,088,115.00 against a bond allocation of $2,669,975.00, an overage of $418,140.00 that Barton Malow proposed to cover from variances in other bond packages.
2014_064_051514spmtg.page:
MEETING
Special Board of Education meeting, Thursday, May 15, 2014, 4:45 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, phone 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Agenda: Pledge of Allegiance; Public Communication; Business items A through C; Other item A; Adjournment.

3.A SECURE ENTRANCES (BID PACKAGE 1 / 9777)
Bid responses for secure entrances at 12 elementary sites, Baker Middle School and International Academy East were reviewed by Kenneth Miller, Executive Director of Maintenance and Operations, and Ronald Curtis, Senior Project Manager, Barton Malow. Awards are to be charged to the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

| Category | Contractor | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 061000 General Trades | Construction Solutions, Inc. | $1,892,300.00 |
| 230000 Mechanical | Miller-Boldt, Inc. | $636,815.00 |
| 260000 Electrical | Metro Electric Engineering Technologies, Inc. | $559,000.00 |
| Total Bid | | $3,088,115.00 |

BUDGET
The bond application allocated $2,669,975.00. The bids equaled $3,088,115.00, which was $418,140.00 over the projected cost, to be funded from variances in other packages. The end budget amount of $51,360 from the roofing project at Larson and Boulan Park Middle Schools can be applied at this point. Barton Malow states an intent to manage the over/unders to at least a net zero add to the bond issue.

BIDDING NOTES
Proposals were received May 1, 2014. Only one bid was received for general trades; three of four committed contractors dropped out citing inability to staff the project. Firms that backed out are listed as Arjac Inc., M.L. Schoenherr, NACE and Precision Contracting. The apparent low electrical bidder, Ecker Mechanical, asked to withdraw claiming its bid was incomplete; Barton Malow recommends allowing withdrawal and awarding to second low bidder Metro Electric, noting a bid bond claim would delay the project and might recover approximately $10,000. Group 1 buildings are Costello, Hill Leonard, Martel, Morse and Wattles; Group 2 are Barnard, Bemis, Hamilton, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wass, Baker MS and IAE.

3.B / 3.C IPAD CASES
On April 22, 2014 the board awarded a portion of the bid for Computer Equipment, Mobile Devices and Accessories for Gumdrop Tech iPad cases to CDWG in the amount of $153,000. Mark Washington, Director of Technology, learned of the MaxCase Shield case at a Michigan School Business Officials conference. The Shield costs $23 per unit compared with $30 per unit for the Gumdrop, a savings of $35,700, and has two open slots in the back for barcode and ID labels. The resolutions rescind the $153,000 CDWG award and award 5100 iPad MaxCase Shield cases at $23 each for a total of $117,300.00, expensed from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

4.A OAKLAND SCHOOLS BIENNIAL ELECTION
Under Public Act 419 of 2004 the Troy Board must designate a representative to the electoral body and identify the candidate it supports. One candidate filed, incumbent George Ehlert, running unopposed for one six-year seat ending June 30, 2020. Balloting is in person, 5:30 to 7:30 PM, Monday, June 2, 2014, Conference Room A, Oakland Schools, 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford. Resolutions may be adopted no earlier than May 12, 2014 and copies are due to Oakland Schools by Friday, May 30, 2014.
2014_064_051514spmtg.verbose:
Special Board of Education meeting agenda for Thursday, May 15, 2014, called for 4:45 PM at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, phone 248.823.4000. The masthead notes that board meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and may be viewed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Business, consisting of A. Bond Project Bid Approval Bid Pkg. 1 Secure Entrances/Other, B. iPad Cases Bid Retraction, and C. Purchase of iPad Cases; 4. Other, consisting of A. Adoption of Oakland Schools Biennial Election Resolution; and 5. Adjournment. Public participation is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, with each person allowed up to three minutes, subject to reduction by the President when the number of speakers exceeds the time limit.

ITEM 3.A, SECURE ENTRANCES. Bid responses for secure entrances at 12 elementary sites, Baker Middle School and International Academy East were reviewed by Mr. Kenneth Miller, Executive Director of Maintenance and Operations, and Mr. Ronald Curtis, Senior Project Manager, Barton Malow. The suggested resolution awards the bid and approves the amounts as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund: Construction Solutions, Inc., General Trades, $1,892,300.00; Miller-Boldt, Inc., Mechanical, $636,815.00; Metro Electric Engineering Technologies, Inc., Electrical, $559,000.00; Total Bid $3,088,115.00.

A memorandum dated 12 May 2014 from Kenneth D. Miller, Executive Director, Facility Operations and Purchasing Department, 1140 Rankin, Troy, Michigan 48083, phone 248 823-4050, fax 248 823-4077, addressed to Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent Business Services, and subject-lined Secure Entrance under the Bond Renovation Project, states that after analyzing the proposals and attending the post bid reviews Miller concurs with Barton Malow's recommendation on bid package 9777, Secure Entrance at all 12 elementary sites, Baker and International Academy East, listing Construction Solutions, Inc. (General Trades) $1,892,300.00, Miller-Boldt, Inc. (Mechanical) $636,815.00, and Metro Electric Engineering Technologies, Inc. (Electrical) $559,000.00. Based on the bond application the funding allocated was $2,669,975.00; the bids equaled $3,088,115.00, which was $418,140.00 over the projected cost. Miller attributes part of the overage to the tight timeline needed to start the projects during summer 2014, noting that projects of this magnitude would normally be bid 6 to 8 months before construction kickoff but that the bond did not go up for vote until November of 2013, leaving only a couple of months to process. General Trades firms that initially planned to provide proposals but backed out due to a last minute addendum and other obligations already scheduled for summer 2014 are listed as Arjac Inc., M.L. Schoenherr, NACE and Precision Contracting. Copies went to Pat Orczykowski, Business Department, and the Purchasing Department file.

A letter dated May 12, 2014 from Barton Malow Company, 26500 American Drive, Southfield, Michigan 48034, phone 248.4365000, fax 248.436.5001, to Mr. Kenneth Miller, Executive Director, Troy School District, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, covers the 2013 Bond Program, Series 1, Bid Package 1, Secure Entrance Remodeling at 14 Buildings, and contract award recommendations. The project scope describes a Welcome Center/secure entrance concept in which a visitor enters the main building entrance vestibule through exterior doors left open to permit vestibule-only access for shelter in inclement weather, sees a glazed wall and door leading from the vestibule directly to the main office, and finds the inner set of vestibule doors locked to prevent further passage into the school. The visitor communicates with the main office secretary from the vestibule over an audiovisual station, is identified and permitted access to the main office, completes identification and sign-in with the secretary, and then enters the school through a separate door beyond the secure entrance.

Proposals were received on May 1, 2014. Barton Malow recommends contracts as follows: category 061000 General Trades, Construction Solutions, Inc., $1,892,300; category 230000 Mechanical, Miller-Boldt, Inc., $636,815; category 260000 Electrical, Metro Electric Engineering Technologies, Inc., $559,000; total $3,088,115. Under Special Considerations the letter notes that only one bid was received for the general trades category, that four contractors were committed to bidding until the last days of the bidding period, and that the three that dropped out cited inability to staff the project if awarded a contract. Barton Malow states that although it would typically not recommend making an award from a single bid, in this case it does not see the situation improving because most contractors have their work load set for the summer this late in the bidding season, and that with the bond issue approved in November the architect/engineer was not able to start design work and produce bid packages for the January/February time frame the firm would prefer. The letter also reports that the apparent low bidder for electrical work, Ecker Mechanical, requested that its bid be withdrawn claiming the bid was incomplete, and recommends allowing the withdrawal and awarding to the second low bidder, Metro Electric, because attempting to recover damages from the bid bond would delay the project and may only result in a recovery of approximately $10,000. Under Budget, the letter states the budget for this work is $2,669,975, resulting in an overage of $418,140 which will be funded from variances in other packages, that the end budget amount of $51,360 from the roofing project at Larson and Boulan Park Middle Schools can be applied at this point, and that going forward Barton Malow intends to manage the over/unders to at least a net zero add to the bond issue. The letter is signed by the Senior Project Manager, with a bid tabulation attached and a copy to Ms. Nichol Bruno, BMC.

The attached bid tabulation is headed Troy School District, 2013 Bond Program, Series 1, Bid Package 1: Secure Entrances at 14 Buildings, with columns for Base Bid (Group 1), Base Bid (Group 2), Combined Bid (Group 1 and 2), Alternate 1 (Group 2), Alternate 2 (Group 1), Alternate 2 (Group 2), Addendum 1,2,3, Bid Bond, Family Disclosure Form, Clarifications Included, and Comments and Voluntary Alternates. Notes define Group 1 as Costello, Hill Leonard, Martel, Morse and Wattles, and Group 2 as Barnard, Bemis, Hamilton, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wass, Baker MS and IAE. In bid category 061000 General Trades, Construction Solutions bid $1,137,600 for Group 1, $774,700 for Group 2, $1,892,300 combined, $156,700 for Alternate 1 (Group 2), $41,000 for Alternate 2 (Group 1), and no bid on Alternate 2 (Group 2). In bid category 230000 Mechanical, Miller-Boldt bid $371,315 and $265,500 with no combined bid and a voluntary alternate to deduct $10,000 to use Carrier equipment and Carrier fan coils; Ecker Mechanical Contractors Inc. bid $398,600 and $296,100; Johnson and Wood bid $431,540 and $326,790 with a combined bid of $744,100; Contrast Mechanical bid $443,133 and $319,605 with a combined bid of $762,738. In bid category 260000 Electrical, Ecker Mechanical Contractors Inc. bid $218,500 and $244,100; Metro Electric Engineering Technologies bid $291,000 and $268,000; Great Lakes Power and Lighting bid $292,000 and $296,000.

ITEM 3.B, IPAD CASES BID RETRACTION. On April 22, 2014 the Board of Education awarded a portion of the bid for Computer Equipment, Mobile Devices and Accessories for Gumdrop Tech iPad cases to CDWG in the amount of $153,000. The district subsequently learned of a newly introduced iPad case, the Shield, from MaxCase, which provides the same level of protection as the Gumdrop cases and offers other benefits at $23 per unit compared with $30 per unit for the Gumdrop case, a savings for the district of $35,700. The suggested resolution rescinds the $153,000 CDWG award. A supporting memorandum dated May 8, 2014 from Mark Washington, Director of Technology, to Dr. Barbara Fowler, Superintendent, explains that he learned of the Shield after attending the most recent Michigan School Business Officials conference, that the case has two open slots in the back usable for barcode and ID labels so a case can be inventoried and identified without turning the device on, and that the case costs $23 per unit instead of $30 per unit for a savings of $35,700. The Gumdrop cases had been selected off the National Joint Purchasing Association (NJPA) bid vehicle; Gumdrop had not been notified of the award, so there were no vendor issues. All cases are in stock from MaxCase of California and MaxCases are also available via the NJPA bid vehicle. Lansing Public Schools has used an earlier model for two years with success, and another MaxCase product was named by District Administration Magazine readers as one of the Top 100 Products of 2013. Washington recommends 5100 iPad MaxCase Shield Cases at $23 each for a total of $117,300, expensed from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

ITEM 3.C, IPAD CASES PURCHASE. The companion resolution awards the bid for iPad Shield cases to MaxCase in the amount of $117,300.00 as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

ITEM 4.A, BIENNIAL ELECTION FOR OAKLAND SCHOOLS BOARD OF EDUCATION ON JUNE 2, 2014. In accordance with Public Act 419 of 2004 the Troy Board of Education must elect members to the Oakland Schools Board of Education and select a designate to cast a ballot on its behalf. The board is to designate a representative and discuss the candidate, Mr. George Ehlert, an incumbent running unopposed for the one open seat. The resolution recites that Public Act 419 of 2004 amended election procedures for intermediate school districts, requires a constituent board to designate its representative and identify the supported candidate by resolution adopted not earlier than 21 days prior to the election, and requires consideration at not less than one public meeting before adoption, with the Troy board considering the resolution at an open meeting under the Open Meetings Act on May 15, 2014. The operative paragraphs designate a representative to the 2014 electoral body, state support for a candidate for one position for a term of six years ending June 30, 2020, and direct the representative to vote for that candidate at least on the first ballot taken at the June 2 election. A certification block is provided for the Secretary of the Board of Education of Troy, Michigan.

An attached email dated Thursday, May 08, 2014, 9:29:43 AM from Kathy Boike, Executive Assistant, Office of the Superintendent and Board of Education, Oakland Schools, 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford, MI 48328, phone 248.209.2123, fax 248.209.2206, reports that one individual filed for the one open seat, Mr. George Ehlert for a 6-year term. Attachments include a Local Board Resolution Template, the OS BOE 2014 Election Timeline Revised, and MCL 380.614. The email explains that Oakland Schools board members are elected by an electoral body composed of one person designated by each constituent district board, that designated electors must cast ballots in person between 5:30 and 7:30 PM on Monday, June 2, 2014 in Conference Room A of the Oakland Schools building at 2111 Pontiac Lake Road in Waterford, and that absentee ballots are prohibited. It describes three options districts have used to consider and adopt resolutions, notes that resolutions may be adopted no earlier than twenty-one days prior to the election, that is, no earlier than May 12, 2014, and asks that adopted resolutions be faxed to 248.209.2206 by the end of business on Friday, May 30, 2014. Questions may be directed to Sherry McMillan at 248.209.2062. Because the candidate is an unopposed incumbent, no Meet the Candidates forum will be scheduled.

The attached Oakland Schools Board of Education Election 2014 Timeline lists: March 12 to May 5, candidates may pick up nominating petitions and affidavit forms at the Oakland County Clerk's office, Elections Division, 1200 N. Telegraph Road, Dept. 417, Pontiac, 48341; Monday, May 5, 4 PM, last day to file nominating petitions, filing fees and affidavits of identity; Thursday, May 8, Oakland Schools receives the list of qualified candidates and forwards it to constituent district superintendents and board secretaries; May 12 to May 29, each constituent board designates its representative, identifies supported candidates, and considers and adopts a resolution, with consideration at not less than one public meeting before adoption; Friday, May 30, copies of district resolutions due via fax 248.209.2206 or email to Kathy.Boike@oakland.k12.mi.us; Monday, June 2, 5:30 to 7:30 PM, representatives cast ballots at the Oakland Schools Board of Education open meeting with no absentee ballots accepted; Tuesday, June 3, notification of results sent to district superintendents and the Oakland County Clerk; Monday, July 14, successful candidates take the oath of office at the Oakland Schools Board of Education Organizational Meeting.

2014_065_060314mtg.paragraph: Agenda and backup for the regular Troy Board of Education meeting of June 3, 2014, held at 7:00 PM at Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085. The agenda opens with an unusually long recognition block covering winter All-State athletes, senior scholar athletes and dozens of academic and arts competitions, then moves to two elementary principal appointments, a resolution setting a public hearing on the proposed 2014-2015 budget, and a bond bid award. Parking lot and walkway lighting at seven elementary buildings was recommended for award to McNulty Electric, Inc. in the amount of $342,700.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.
2014_065_060314mtg.page:
MEETING
Regular meeting, June 3, 2014, 7:00 PM, Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085. Board offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000. Items may be taken out of order, and consent agenda items are acted on at one time unless removed.

RECOGNITIONS
The recognition block runs from item A through item QQQ and includes All-State Athletes for winter sports, Senior Scholar Athletes for winter and spring sports, the Sodexo Future Chef Award 2014, Best Communities in Music Education, the Troy Community Coalition Incredible Kid Award, and competition honors including the American Mathematics Competition, Chemistry Olympiad, C-SPAN StudentCam, DECA, Destination ImagiNation, Future Problem Solvers, MATHCOUNTS, Michigan Youth Arts Festival, National French, Japanese and Spanish Exams, Scholastic Art and Writing Awards, First Tech Challenge Robotics, Robofest World Championship Qualifiers, National History Day, USA Mathematical Olympiad, USA Biology Olympiad, Model UN, the Siemens Competition in Math, Science, and Technology, and the Intel International Science and Engineering Fair.

6.A PERSONNEL - PRINCIPAL, BARNARD ELEMENTARY
Ms. Melanie O'Neil is recommended for appointment. She comes from the Grosse Pointe Public School System where she was Principal of Kerby Elementary School for 2 years, and previously spent 19 years with Lake Orion Community Schools as Director of Early Childhood Programs for 4 years, Elementary Principal for 4 years and a teacher for 11 years. Bachelor's degree, Central Michigan University, 1992; Master's in Educational Administration, Michigan State University, 1997. Duties begin July 1, 2014.

6.B PERSONNEL - PRINCIPAL, HAMILTON ELEMENTARY
Ms. Sarah Glasser is recommended for appointment. She comes from Hamtramck Public Schools where she was Principal of Dickinson East Elementary School for 3 years after 2 years as Assistant Principal there, and taught in the same system for 11 years, a total of 16 years with Hamtramck Public Schools. Bachelor's degree, The University of Michigan, 1992; Master's in Educational Leadership, DePaul University, 1998. Duties begin July 1, 2014.

8.A BUDGET PUBLIC HEARING RESOLUTION
Michigan law requires a public hearing on the proposed budget with notice at least six days beforehand, stating the time, place and where the budget may be inspected, and including in 11-point bold faced type the statement that the property tax millage rate proposed to be levied to support the proposed budget will be a subject of the hearing. The resolution sets the hearing for June 17, 2014 at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098. Exhibit A, the publication notice, states copies of the proposed budget will be available at the Administrative Building, 4400 Livernois, from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., Wednesday, June 11, 2014 through Tuesday, June 17, 2014, and is signed by Karl D. Schmidt, Secretary, Board of Education.

Award recommended to McNulty Electric, Inc. for $342,700.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Barton Malow's May 29, 2014 letter covers Bid Package 3A of the 2013 Bond Program Series 1; proposals were received May 27, 2014, the budget for the work is $343,000, and the buildings are Barnard, Costello, Martell, Morse, Troy Union, Wass and Wattles.

ITEM 6.A, ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, PRINCIPAL, BARNARD ELEMENTARY SCHOOL. The superintendent recommends the appointment of Ms. Melanie O'Neil as Principal of Barnard Elementary School. O'Neil comes to the Troy School District from the Grosse Pointe Public School System, where she has been the Principal of Kerby Elementary School for 2 years. Prior to Grosse Pointe she spent 19 years with Lake Orion Community Schools, working as Director of Early Childhood Programs for 4 years, an Elementary Principal for 4 years, and a teacher for 11 years. She received her Bachelor's degree from Central Michigan University in 1992 and her Master's degree in Educational Administration from Michigan State University in 1997. With board approval she will begin her duties as Principal of Barnard Elementary School as of July 1, 2014. The suggested resolution approves the personnel recommendation.

ITEM 6.B, ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, PRINCIPAL, HAMILTON ELEMENTARY SCHOOL. The superintendent recommends the appointment of Ms. Sarah Glasser as Principal of Hamilton Elementary School. Glasser comes to the Troy School District from Hamtramck Public Schools, where she has been the Principal of Dickinson East Elementary School for 3 years after serving as Assistant Principal of Dickinson East for 2 years. Prior to her administrative assignments she taught in the same school system for 11 years, giving her a total of 16 years with Hamtramck Public Schools. She received her Bachelor's degree from The University of Michigan in 1992 and her Master's degree in Educational Leadership from DePaul University in 1998. With board approval she will begin her duties as Principal of Hamilton Elementary School as of July 1, 2014. The suggested resolution approves the personnel recommendation.

ITEM 8.A, RESOLUTION TO HOLD A PUBLIC HEARING ON THE PROPOSED 2014-2015 SCHOOL YEAR BUDGET. The recitals state that Michigan law provides that every local unit of government, including a school district, shall hold a public hearing on its proposed budget with notice at least six days before the hearing; that the notice must include the time and place of the hearing and state where a copy of the proposed budget is available for public inspection; that the notice must include, in 11-point bold faced type, the statement that the property tax millage rate proposed to be levied to support the proposed budget will be a subject of the hearing; and that each local unit must hold the public hearing prior to final adoption of its budget. The resolution provides that a public hearing shall be held on June 17, 2014 at a regular board meeting beginning at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, for the purpose of receiving testimony and discussing the proposed 2014-2015 budget, and authorizes and directs the Secretary of the Board of Education to publish notice substantially in the form of the attached Exhibit A in a newspaper of general circulation within the school district at least six days before the hearing.

Exhibit A is the publication notice, headed Troy School District Notice of a Public Hearing on the Proposed Budget for the 2014-2015 School Year. It states that the district will hold a public hearing on its proposed budget for the 2014-2015 school year at a regular meeting of the Board of Education at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098, beginning at 7:00 p.m. on Tuesday, June 17, 2014, and that copies of the proposed budget will be available for public inspection at the Administrative Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., Wednesday, June 11, 2014 through Tuesday, June 17, 2014. The millage statement appears in the required 11-point bold faced type. The notice is signed by Karl D. Schmidt, Secretary, Board of Education.

ITEM 8.B, PARKING LOT/WALKWAY LIGHTING. Bid responses for parking lot and walkway lighting at 7 elementary buildings were reviewed by Mr. Kenneth Miller, Executive Director, and Mr. Ronald Curtis, Senior Project Manager, Barton Malow. The suggested resolution awards the bid for parking lot/walkway lighting to McNulty Electric, Inc. in the amount of $342,700.00 and approves that amount as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

Supporting the award is a letter dated May 29, 2014 from Barton Malow Company, 26500 American Drive, Southfield, Michigan 48034, phone 248.4365000, fax 248.436.5001, to Mr. Kenneth Miller, Executive Director, Troy School District, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, regarding the 2013 Bond Program, Series 1, Bid Package 3A, Parking Lot Lighting at 7 Buildings, contract award recommendation. Proposals were received on May 27, 2014 to replace site lighting at 7 elementary schools. The letter notes that contracts were previously awarded for paving work at these buildings to separate bus, parent drop off and pedestrian traffic, and that this lighting package is related to that work. Barton Malow reviewed the proposal and qualifications of the apparent low bidder and recommends a contract in category 260000 Electrical to McNulty Electric, Inc. for $342,700. The bid package includes new site lighting at Barnard, Costello, Martell, Morse, Troy Union, Wass and Wattles. The budget for this work is $343,000. The letter is signed by the Senior Project Manager, with a bid tabulation attached and a copy to Ms. Nichol Bruno, BMC.

The attached bid tabulation, headed Troy School District, 2013 Bond Program, Series 1, Bid Package 3A Parking Lot Lighting Replacement, lists base bids and ranks with bid bond, family disclosure form and clarifications columns: McNulty Electric $342,700, rank 1; Rauhorn Electric $356,396, rank 2; Metro Electric $367,500, rank 3; LaBelle Electric $399,000, rank 4; J Ranck Electric $405,716, rank 5; DoubleJack Electric $407,150, rank 6; and Munro Electric $418,100, rank 7. All seven bidders are shown with a bid bond and family disclosure form and with clarifications not included.

2014_066_061014spmtg.paragraph: Agenda and supporting documents for a special Troy Board of Education meeting on June 10, 2014 at 5:30 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois. Business included the appointment of Mark Dziatczak as Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction, approval of the employment agreement for Superintendent Dr. Richard M. Machesky, an award for Athens High School marching band uniforms, and an award to relocate playground structures at Troy Union and Wass Elementary Schools. The Machesky agreement runs from July 1, 2014 through June 30, 2017 at an annual salary of One Hundred Seventy-Eight Thousand Dollars ($178,000).
2014_066_061014spmtg.page:
MEETING
Special meeting, June 10, 2014, 5:30 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Agenda: Pledge of Allegiance; Public Communication; Personnel; Business; Adjournment.

3.A ASSISTANT SUPERINTENDENT, SECONDARY INSTRUCTION
Mark Dziatczak is recommended for appointment, moving from Principal at Troy High School where he has worked since July 2005, and having previously served as Assistant Principal and Interim Principal at Athens High School. He holds an undergraduate degree in Physics from Wayne State University, a Master's in K-12 Educational Administration from Michigan State University, and an Education Specialist Degree in Educational Leadership from Oakland University, and is enrolled in the Doctoral Program in Education Leadership at Oakland University. The resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, effective July 1, 2014.

3.B SUPERINTENDENT CONTRACT
At the May 6, 2014 meeting, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Ms. Underwood, the board voted unanimously to offer the superintendency to Dr. Richard Machesky. The employment agreement, entered into on June 10, 2014, runs July 1, 2014 through June 30, 2017 without tenure.

Board meeting agenda for a special meeting of the Troy Board of Education on June 10, 2014 at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The masthead gives the district address as 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, phone 248.823.4000, and notes cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streaming at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The agenda lists Pledge of Allegiance, Public Communication, Personnel items A and B, Business items A and B, and Adjournment.

ITEM 3.A, ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, ASSISTANT SUPERINTENDENT, SECONDARY INSTRUCTION. The recommendation is for the appointment of Mark Dziatczak as Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction. Dziatczak comes to the position from Principal at Troy High School, where he has worked since July 2005, and previously worked as an Assistant Principal and Interim Principal at Athens High School. He received his undergraduate degree in Physics from Wayne State University, his Master's Degree in K-12 Educational Administration from Michigan State University, and his Education Specialist Degree in Educational Leadership from Oakland University, and is currently enrolled in the Doctoral Program in Education Leadership at Oakland University. The suggested resolution provides that the Board of Education issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Mr. Mark Dziatczak, who will begin duties as Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction effective July 1, 2014.

ITEM 3.B, SUPERINTENDENT'S CONTRACT APPROVAL. At its May 6, 2014 meeting it was moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Ms. Underwood for the Troy Board of Education to offer the position of Superintendent of Troy School District to Dr. Richard Machesky, and the resolution was approved unanimously. Following successful negotiation of a contract, the board is asked to approve the agreement, which provides a contract through June 30, 2017 commencing July 1, 2014. The suggested resolution approves the contract of the Superintendent of Schools, in effect from July 1, 2014 through June 30, 2017, without tenure in the administrative position and subject to the provisions of the written agreement.

SUPERINTENDENT OF SCHOOLS EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT. The agreement, entered into on June 10, 2014, is between the Board of Education of the Troy School District and Dr. Richard M. Machesky. Paragraph 1, Employment Term, sets the period commencing July 1, 2014 and terminating June 30, 2017, renewable at any time prior to its expiration date of June 30, 2017 by duly authorized written agreement. Paragraph 2, Qualifications, requires the educational qualifications of Section 1246 of the Michigan School Code of 1976 (Public Act 451 of 1976), as amended. Paragraph 3, Duties and Responsibilities, requires the superintendent to serve as directed by the board and as required by Michigan law and to obey and fulfill board policies, rules and regulations. Paragraph 4, Performance Evaluation, requires the board to provide a written evaluation no later than June 1 of each calendar year, with the instrument and evaluation format made known to the superintendent by November 1 of the immediately prior calendar year. Paragraph 5, Salary, sets an annual salary of One Hundred Seventy-Eight Thousand Dollars ($178,000), with the board retaining the right to adjust the salary prospectively but not to reduce it below that figure. Paragraph 6, Work Year, requires performance of duties over the full fifty-two weeks of the district's fiscal year, July 1 through June 30, less applicable vacation, leave and holidays, including attendance at board and committee meetings and district and civic functions, with no additional compensation for such attendance. Paragraph 7, Fringe Benefits, incorporates the attached Fringe Benefit Supplement, subject to annual review for modification by the board. Paragraph 8 bars outside employment or self-employment without prior board consent. Paragraph 9, Conflict of Interest, requires full disclosure of any questioned interest, with the board's disposition controlling, and includes the superintendent's representation that he possesses no interest adverse to the district. Paragraph 10, Residency, states the board prefers district residency but that it is not required.

Paragraph 11, Discipline and Termination, permits discipline, suspension or termination for reasonable and good cause with notice and a fair hearing, defines good cause to include an act of moral turpitude, any misdemeanor or felony criminal conviction or plea of nolo contendere, violation of the agreement, or disability as provided in Paragraph F of the Fringe Benefit Supplement, and requires thirty days written notice and opportunity to cure any curable violation plus opportunity to attend any board meeting at which a termination vote is taken. Paragraph 12, Arbitration, commits all disputes to arbitration under the Employment Rules of the American Arbitration Association, conducted in Oakland County, Michigan, with the parties equally sharing arbitrator fees and hearing room rental, and limits the arbitrator's opinion in a termination case to whether the board had good cause. Paragraph 13, Non-Renewal, leaves the renewal decision solely within the board's discretion but requires at least ninety days written notice of non-renewal prior to expiration; the superintendent may terminate on at least ninety days written notice, which the board may waive in whole or part. Paragraph 14, Tenure Exclusion, provides that no continuing tenure is granted under the Teachers' Tenure Act, Act 4 of the Public Acts of 1937 (Extra Session), as amended. Paragraph 15, Medical Examination, requires an annual medical examination with a written fitness statement provided to the Board President, reimbursement of examination costs not covered by insurance, and reserves the board's right to direct an examination to verify physical or psychological competence, with reports shared by the President with other trustees but otherwise kept confidential. Paragraph 16, Indemnification, requires the board to defend, hold harmless and indemnify the superintendent from claims arising within the scope of employment, excluding criminal proceedings at the board's sole discretion and claims or actions of the district, and excluding alleged intentional tortious actions or inactions; the board must provide public liability insurance at reasonable cost in an aggregate amount of not less than three million dollars ($3,000,000.00) and reimburse expenses and judgments not covered by insurance, with no individual board member personally liable. Paragraph 17, Entire Agreement, states the agreement and Fringe Benefit Supplement contain all terms and that the Administrative Handbook of the Troy School District is not applicable to the superintendent. Paragraph 18, Applicable Law, makes the contract subject to Michigan law with a severability clause. Signature blocks are provided for Dr. Nancy Philippart, Board of Education President, Karl Schmidt, Board of Education Secretary, and Dr. Richard M. Machesky, Superintendent.

FRINGE BENEFIT SUPPLEMENT. Paragraph A provides health, dental and vision insurance on the same single, two-person or full family basis as other administrators, subject to modification. Paragraph B provides long-term disability insurance on the same basis as other administrators, with benefits of sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66-2/3%) of monthly earnings for inability to work due to extended sickness or injury, payable until age seventy (70); monthly earnings include compensation subject to board-paid retirement contributions to the Michigan Public School Employees Retirement System (MPSERS) at the time of disability divided by twelve months, and the coverage has a 365-day waiting period, with insurance amounts reduced by primary remuneration from the board, the Michigan Public School Employee's Retirement Fund and the Federal Social Security Act. Paragraph C provides a group term life insurance policy paying a designated beneficiary a sum equal to $500,000. Paragraph D provides accidental death and dismemberment insurance in the sum of $1,000,000. Paragraph E, Worker's Compensation, requires prompt notice of on-the-job injury and provides that if the superintendent is absent due to a job-related accident he will be paid, for a period not to exceed sixty days from the date of the accident, the difference between full salary and worker's compensation benefits, with no district supplement after entry into long-term disability coverage. Paragraph F, Income Protection, continues salary for temporary incapacity due to illness or disability but not beyond any continuous period of one calendar year, crediting board-paid disability insurance and statutory worker's compensation amounts; after incapacity exceeding twelve calendar months the board may terminate on written notice, after which insurance benefits continue for the remainder of the first year of long-term disability benefits. Paragraph G provides payment of one state, one local and one national association dues at the superintendent's discretion, plus tuition and registration reimbursement for required professional development on the same basis as other administrators. Paragraph H allows reimbursement of reasonable and appropriate business expenses in accordance with the Internal Revenue Code, Internal Revenue guidelines and Michigan Department of Treasury guidelines, with valid receipts and expense reports. Paragraph I provides 25 paid vacation days per fiscal year which may not be carried forward, with payment on termination or non-renewal for prorated unused earned vacation at the pro-rata daily rate (salary divided by 365 days) using the formula number of total vacation days divided by 12 times number of months worked minus used vacation time. Paragraph J provides twelve (12) paid holidays: July 4, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, Friday after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year's Eve, New Year's Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, and two floating holidays during the winter recess, with pay included in salary. Paragraph K permits a tax-sheltered annuity as added compensation but states no annuity will be provided for the 2014-15 fiscal year.
